dana: Customer reporting a burst of 500s + very high p95 around 03:12 UTC. They provided two full request ids: r-abc123def456 and r-abc123def789. Says it happened right after a webhook batch.

marta: thanks — can you ask them to run a tiny reproducible curl and include the exact response headers (we need X-Request-Id + X-Node-ID) and the raw request body? if they can upload the raw output to our bucket that speeds triage.

dana: pasted redacted customer note: \"POST /v1/generate -> 500, body: {\\\"error\\\":\\\"internal\\\"}, first-byte ~3.6s, retried once. model redwood-3b, prompt ~40 tokens. auth via api key.\"

oncall-bot: trace lookup: r-abc123def456 routed to host gpu-27, trace shows model-init 1.6s then retry to runtime; backend returned 502 then 500; kv-cache eviction 03:09:58 UTC on that node.

liam: quick curl to ask them to run (ask them to add -D to save headers and -v for TLS/conn timings):

curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -H \"X-Debug: trace\" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"Summarize: incident observed","max_tokens":48}'

liam: instruct them to run with `-D /tmp/ri_hdrs.txt -o /tmp/ri_body.txt -v` and paste the headers file or upload to s3.

nina: python (requests) minimal snippet — include timeout and print headers: 

```python
import os
import requests
url = \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\"
headers = {\"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY')}\", \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\", \"X-Debug\": \"trace\"}
json = {\"model\": \"redwood-3b\", \"input\": \"Summarize: incident observed\", \"max_tokens\": 48}
try:
  r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=json, timeout=15)
  print(r.status_code)
  print(dict(r.headers))
  print(r.text)
except Exception as e:
  print('err', e)
```

sasha: node example (fetch):

```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async ()=>{
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method:'POST',
    headers:{'Authorization':`Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`,'Content-Type':'application/json','X-Debug':'trace'},
    body: JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-3b', input:'Summarize: incident observed', max_tokens:48}),
    timeout:15000
  });
  console.log(res.status, Object.fromEntries(res.headers));
  console.log(await res.text());
})();
```

jamal: go example (ops-friendly):

```go
package main
import (
  \"bytes\"
  \"fmt\"
  \"io/ioutil\"
  \"net/http\"
  \"os\"
)
func main(){
  client := &http.Client{}
  reqBody := []byte(`{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"Summarize: incident observed","max_tokens":48}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest(\"POST\",\"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\", bytes.NewReader(reqBody))
  req.Header.Set(\"Authorization\",\"Bearer \"+os.Getenv(\"REDWOOD_KEY\"))
  req.Header.Set(\"Content-Type\",\"application/json\")
  req.Header.Set(\"X-Debug\",\"trace\")
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err!=nil{ fmt.Println(\"err\",err); return }
  b,_ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.Status)
  fmt.Println(resp.Header)
  fmt.Println(string(b))
}
```

marta: tiny one-liner that saves headers/body and uploads to support bucket (assumes aws cli configured):

curl -s -D /tmp/ri_hdrs.txt -o /tmp/ri_body.txt -w \"http_code:%{http_code} time_total:%{time_total}\\n\" \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -H \"X-Debug: trace\" \\
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"Summarize: incident observed","max_tokens":48}' && \\
aws s3 cp /tmp/ri_hdrs.txt s3://redwood-support-artifacts/1859991234/ --acl private && aws s3 cp /tmp/ri_body.txt s3://redwood-support-artifacts/1859991234/ --acl private

marta: tell them to paste the exact X-Request-Id returned (we need full header value), and the s3 paths. that lets us pull traces and match server logs.
